audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Elijah ascent and Elisha succession narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Gilgal-Bethel-Jericho-Jordan itinerary, sons of prophets, Elijah's ascent, double-portion request, mantle/Jordan sign, Jericho water healing, and bears episode.

verses.restored: When YHWH was about to take Elijah up in storm-wind to heavens, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.
Elijah said to Elisha, Stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me to Bethel. Elisha said, As YHWH lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. So they went down to Bethel.
Sons of prophets at Bethel came to Elisha and said, Do you know that today YHWH is taking your master from over your head? He said, I also know; be silent.
Elijah said, Elisha, stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me to Jericho. He said, As YHWH lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. So they came to Jericho.
Sons of prophets at Jericho came to Elisha and said, Do you know that today YHWH is taking your master from over your head? He said, I also know; be silent.
Elijah said, Stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me to Jordan. He said, As YHWH lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. So the two of them went.
Fifty men from sons of prophets went and stood opposite at a distance, while the two stood by Jordan.
Elijah took his mantle, rolled it, struck waters, and they divided here and there; the two crossed on dry ground.
When they crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you. Elisha said, Let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.
He said, You have asked a hard thing. If you see me being taken from you, it shall be so; if not, it shall not be.
As they were walking and speaking, look, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in storm-wind to heavens.
Elisha was seeing and cried, My father, my father! Chariot of Israel and its horsemen! He saw him no more. He grasped his clothes and tore them in two pieces.
He lifted Elijah's mantle that had fallen from upon him and returned and stood on bank of Jordan.
He took Elijah's mantle that had fallen and struck waters, saying, Where is YHWH, Divine of Elijah? He struck waters, and they divided here and there, and Elisha crossed.
Sons of prophets at Jericho saw him opposite and said, Spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha. They came to meet him and bowed to ground before him.
They said, Look, there are with your servants fifty strong men; let them go seek your master, lest Spirit of YHWH lifted him and cast him on some mountain or valley. He said, Do not send.
They pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said, Send. They sent fifty men, searched three days, and did not find him.
They returned to him while he stayed at Jericho, and he said, Did I not say to you, Do not go?
Men of city said to Elisha, Look, dwelling of city is good, as my lord sees, but waters are bad and land miscarries/bereaves.
He said, Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it. They brought it to him.
He went out to spring of waters, threw salt there, and said, Thus says YHWH: I have healed these waters; no more shall death or miscarriage/bereavement come from there.
Waters were healed to this day, according to word of Elisha that he spoke.
He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up by road, small youths came out from city and mocked him, saying, Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!
He turned behind him, saw them, and cursed them in name of YHWH. Two female bears came out from forest and tore forty-two of the youths.
He went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there returned to Samaria.

translation_notes: Elisha's refusal to leave Elijah is fidelity at a death/succession threshold, not permission to deny another person's boundaries in ordinary relationships.
The sons of prophets know loss is coming; Elisha's repeated 'be silent' may mark grief too raw for public processing.
The double portion evokes firstborn inheritance language and succession responsibility, not a request to be twice as impressive.
Elijah's ascent is visionary succession narrative; it should not be used to deny death, grief, or burial for others.
Jericho's water healing addresses public health, fertility of land, and communal survival; miracle language must not replace environmental responsibility or medical care.
The bears episode is morally dangerous. Mockery does not justify child harm, animal attack, cursing children, or violent retaliation by spiritual leaders.
The term often rendered 'boys' or 'youths' is debated, but any age reading requires anti-child-harm safeguards.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 2 to justify cursing children, violence for mockery, denial of grief, leader cult succession, or miracle claims that replace public-health action. Center faithful succession, honest mourning, healed water, and the absolute refusal to make the bears episode a model for spiritual authority.
